description_en: Situated at the Bhelāchẽ Square, this narrow Phalcā was donated by the family of the striking pink house that the Phalcā is embedded into. Facing north, Bhelāchẽ Phalcā stands right in front of asataḥin Bhelāchẽ, near the alleyway that leads from the Thalbuṃ Slope (Thalbuṃ Phalcā) all the way to Kvaylāchi, Cyāsal.Once decorated with tiles, Bhelāchẽ Phalcā was reconstructed as a concrete Phalcā with a terrace on top. The main entrance to the residential house passes through the Phalcā. The house itself has suffered major cracks due to the earthquake and has been declared unlivable, which puts the Phalcā in danger too. Bhelāchẽ Phalcāis owned by a Khusaḥ (Taṇḍukār) family. According to Mr Tandukar (2018 CE), it was built to provide a cool place for those passing by to rest temporarily and take shelter from the heat. According to the present owner of the house, the Phalcā once had a tiled roof and stretched all the way through to another house attached to the west of his residence. This half of the Phalcāwas lost when the second house was rebuilt some years ago. The space previously occupied by this half of the Bhelāchẽ Phalcā is still there, but the owner chose not to rebuild it. Instead, planks have been laid on the floor. The entrance to the house was at the centre of this Phalcā.Open from three sides (east, north and west), the Phalcā now stands on four concrete pillars and is surmounted by a concrete slab that serves as a terrace. The owner informed researchers that Bhelāchẽ Phalcā was previously in a terrible condition and was on the verge of collapse. It was for this reason that it was dismantled and rebuilt in the present structure around 20 years ago. He was worried that the Phalcā was tilting forwards, and feared it would have brought the whole house down with it if it collapsed. The house is built in mud-mortar with one concrete floor on the fourth storey. He believes that this was one of the main reasons the house sustained so much damage during the 2015 earthquakes.
description_ne: भलाछेँ चोकमा च्यासल क्वय्लाछि जाने गल्लीपट्टि तीन वटा कवल भएको उत्तर फर्किएको यो फल्चा कङ्क्रिटले बनेको छ । निर्माण गरी दान गर्ने परिवारको घरसँगै यो फल्चा जोडिएको छ । अहिले यो फल्चाको छत ढलान गरिएको छ । पूर्व, उत्तर र पश्चिम तीनै तर्फ खुला रहेको यो फल्चामा चार वटा कङ्क्रिट पिल्लर छन् । पछाडिको घरभित्र प्रवेश गर्न फल्चा हुँदै जानु पर्छ । २०१५ को भूकम्पमा परी फल्चा पछाडिको घर बेसरी चर्किएको छ ।
monument_assessment: Heavily damaged (collapsed, demolished, major cracks and structural damages)

historical_events.event_description: The construction of Bhelāchẽ Phalcā was funded by a Khusaḥ (Taṇḍukār) family, the descendents of Mangal Tandukar. However, Mr. Tandukar could not remember the name of his ancestor who actually commissioned the Phalcā. According to the house owner, the Phalcā was rebuilt some 20 years ago (around 1995/2000 CE). Niels Gutschow estimates 1980 to be the date of reconstruction, but this could not be confirmed.

The Phalcā was in a bad condition and on the verge of collapse. Mr Tandukar had it dismantled and rebuilt in its present structure in the late 1990s. The Bhelāchẽ Phalcā was converted into a concrete Phalcā with a terrace on top.
